name: Barzillai
bio:
Barzillai the Gileadite, from Rogelim, was among those who brought beds, food, and supplies to David and his exhausted people when they reached Mahanaim fleeing Absalom's rebellion, joining Shobi son of Nahash and Machir son of Ammiel in this timely provision (2 Samuel 17:27-29).

When David returned to Jerusalem after Absalom's defeat, the now eighty-year-old Barzillai came down to the Jordan to see him off. David, grateful for his generosity, invited him to come live at the palace in Jerusalem, but Barzillai declined, saying he was too old to enjoy good food, music, or anything else the king's house could offer, and asked only to be allowed to go home and die near the graves of his parents. He asked David instead to take his son (or companion) Chimham in his place; David agreed, kissed Barzillai, blessed him, and let him return home (2 Samuel 19:31-39). Among David's final instructions to Solomon was a charge to show continued kindness to Barzillai's sons, letting them eat at his table, in gratitude for how their father had sustained David when he fled from Absalom (1 Kings 2:7).
